title: KVGuard：面向 LLM 服务系统的 KV Cache 安全检查器
author: byoungyoung
content:
Computer Science > Cryptography and Security

arXiv:2611.06138 (cs)
[Submitted on 4 Nov 2026]
Authors:Jonguk Cheong, Myungbin Hwang, Eulgyu Kim, Byoungyoung Lee
View PDF HTML (experimental)
Abstract:Modern LLM serving systems manage the KV cache through PagedAttention, a custom GPU allocator that partitions a single CUDA-allocated region into fixed-size physical blocks and maps each request to those blocks through a CPU-built block table. This block-based design exposes a previously unstudied class of memory safety bugs in the KV cache, including double-free, use-after-free, out-of-bounds access, uninitialized read, and permission violation, which silently corrupt outputs or break request isolation without ever crashing the system. Existing memory sanitizers cannot detect them, because they reason about CUDA-level addresses rather than KV cache blocks, requests, and block tables, and their redzone- and quarantine-based designs do not fit the scarce GPU memory budget of LLM serving. This paper presents KVGuard, the first systematic memory-safety abstraction for KV cache management in LLM serving systems. KVGuard maintains a compact shadow block for each physical KV block, recording per-request permission and per-entry initialization, and uses this metadata to perform five safety checks across the PagedAttention workflow, spanning CPU allocation, block table construction and translation, and GPU-side block table lookup and KV entry access. Each check fires at the boundary that introduced the violation, enabling early detection during development rather than reporting downstream output corruption many requests later. A prototype of KVGuard on vLLM and SGLang covers all 29 historical real-world KV cache safety bugs collected from the two systems' patch histories. KVGuard further found 8 previously unknown safety violations while reporting no false positives. It adds 3.0% and 7.4% geomean TPOT overhead on Qwen 2.5 14B on vLLM and SGLang and at most 0.11% of the KV cache in memory overhead, two orders of magnitude below NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer on the same workloads.

summary: 本文介绍了 KVGuard，这是首个针对 LLM 服务系统中 KV Cache 管理的系统化内存安全抽象。现代 LLM 服务使用 PagedAttention 将 GPU 内存划分为固定大小的物理块，并通过由 CPU 构建的块表进行映射。这种设计会引发多类内存安全漏洞，包括重复释放、释放后使用、越界访问、未初始化读取和权限违规；这些问题会在不导致程序崩溃的情况下悄然破坏输出。现有 CUDA 级别的内存检查器无法检测此类漏洞。KVGuard 为每个物理 KV 块维护一个紧凑的影子块，记录每个请求的权限和每个条目的初始化状态，并在 PagedAttention 工作流程中执行 5 项安全检查。基于 vLLM 和 SGLang 的原型覆盖了全部 29 个历史真实 KV Cache 安全漏洞，并在没有误报的情况下发现了 8 个此前未知的违规问题。在 Qwen 2.5 14B 上，其几何平均 TPOT 开销分别为 3.0% 和 7.4%，KV Cache 内存开销最高为 0.11%，比 NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer 低两个数量级。

mainPoints.point: PagedAttention 中的 KV Cache 内存安全漏洞
mainPoints.explanation: PagedAttention 的分块设计会引发多类内存安全漏洞，包括重复释放、释放后使用、越界访问、未初始化读取和权限违规。这些漏洞会在不导致程序崩溃的情况下悄然破坏输出，而现有 CUDA 级别的内存检查器无法检测它们。
KVGuard 为每个物理 KV 块维护一个紧凑的影子块，记录每个请求的权限和每个条目的初始化状态，从而能够在 CPU 分配、块表构建和 GPU 端块查找过程中执行 5 项安全检查。

mainPoints.point: 在 vLLM 和 SGLang 上的实证验证
mainPoints.explanation: 该原型覆盖了从两个系统的补丁历史中收集的全部 29 个历史真实 KV Cache 安全漏洞，在没有误报的情况下发现了 8 个此前未知的违规问题；TPOT 开销仅为 3.0%-7.4%，内存开销为 0.11%。
